text: Managed Kubernetes service (CKS) that runs customer clusters on bare-metal servers in CoreWeave Cloud
quote: CoreWeave Kubernetes Service (CKS) offers a managed Kubernetes service that lets you run clusters on bare metal servers in CoreWeave Cloud.

text: Kubernetes runs directly on bare-metal nodes with no hypervisor; customer clusters don't run VMs
quote: CKS runs Kubernetes directly on bare metal Nodes, without a hypervisor. Customer clusters don't run Virtual Machines.

text: Create clusters through the Cloud Console or with Terraform
quote: You can create a cluster with the Cloud Console or with Terraform.

text: Public API to create, list, update, and delete managed Kubernetes clusters
quote: The API lets you create, list, update, and delete managed Kubernetes clusters on CoreWeave infrastructure.

text: Terraform provider manages CKS clusters, VPC networking, object storage buckets and policies, and Managed Inference as code
quote: The CoreWeave Terraform provider lets you manage CoreWeave infrastructure as code, including CKS clusters, VPC networking, AI Object Storage policies and buckets, and Managed Inference resources.

text: CoreWeave Terraform provider works in OpenTofu configurations
quote: Use the CoreWeave Terraform provider in your OpenTofu configuration.

text: Generated API clients for Connect, gRPC, and Protobuf in Go, Python, TypeScript, Java, Kotlin, Rust, and Swift
quote: Clients are available for the Connect, gRPC, and Protobuf ecosystems across languages including Go, Python, TypeScript, Java, Kotlin, Rust, and Swift.

text: Create and download a kubeconfig for a cluster so you can use kubectl against it
quote: Create and download a kubeconfig for a specific cluster, so you can interact with the cluster using commands like kubectl.

text: API access tokens authenticate users to the API and kubectl, granting access to CKS clusters and VPCs
quote: This page explains how to create, use, and manage API Access Tokens and the kubeconfig files generated alongside them, so you can authenticate kubectl to CKS clusters and keep credentials secure.

text: Run multiple node pools of any size in one cluster to put different workloads on different node types and scale them independently
quote: You can deploy multiple Node Pools within a single cluster, where each Node Pool contains any number of Nodes. This lets you run different types of workloads on different types of Nodes, or scale different parts of your application independ

text: Node pools group instances that share a common configuration, including labels, taints, and annotations
quote: A Node Pool in CKS represents one or more instances that share a common configuration, such as the same labels, taints, and annotations.

text: Kubernetes Cluster Autoscaler scales node pools based on GPU, CPU, or memory demand
quote: CKS supports scaling Node Pools by using the Kubernetes Cluster Autoscaler, letting you scale CKS Node Pools in response to workload demands for GPU, CPU, or memory resources.

text: Spot node pools give pay-as-you-go bare-metal compute without long-term commitments or reservations
quote: Spot Node Pools provide pay-as-you-go access to high-performance bare-metal compute resources without long-term commitments or reservations.

text: On-demand GPU instances let you spin up burst capacity without long-term commitments
quote: Utilize on-demand GPU instances for additional workloads when you're not looking for long-term capacity commitments. Quickly spin-up burst On-Demand or Spot capacity

text: Capacity Finder compares placement availability across zones for GPU and CPU instance types and node counts
quote: use Capacity Finder in the Cloud Console to compare placement availability across Zones for one or more GPU and CPU instance types

text: View quotas in the Console, read quota errors for node pools, and request increases
quote: This page shows you how to view your quotas in the Cloud Console, how to read quota errors when a Node Pool exceeds its quota, and how to request an increase when you need more capacity.

text: Bare-metal GPU nodes with DPU isolation and InfiniBand networking
quote: CoreWeave Kubernetes Service runs your clusters directly on bare-metal GPU Nodes, with DPU isolation, per-cluster VPCs, and InfiniBand networking

text: Each CKS cluster runs inside its own private VPC
quote: CKS is built to offer granular control, high performance, enhanced security, and high reliability...Each CKS cluster operates within its own private Virtual Private Cloud (VPC).

text: SUNK runs Slurm on Kubernetes so batch training and Kubernetes inference workloads share the same GPU pool
quote: CoreWeave SUNK runs Slurm on Kubernetes, letting both batch training jobs and Kubernetes inference workloads share the same GPU pool.

text: Inference API controls inference gateways, model deployments, capacity claims, and checkpoint hot-loads for RL rollouts
quote: provides programmatic control over inference gateways, model deployments, capacity claims, and checkpoint hot-loads for RL Rollouts

text: The Inference API can be called over several transport protocols
quote: You can call the Inference API over several transport protocols, depending on your client tooling and performance needs

text: S3-compatible object storage keeps training data, checkpoints, and model weights close to GPU compute
quote: Store training data, checkpoints, and model weights with efficient S3-compatible access directly to your GPU compute resources.

text: Browse, upload, download, and manage storage objects in the Cloud Console without CLI tools
quote: browse, upload, download, and manage objects in CoreWeave AI Object Storage buckets directly from the CoreWeave Cloud Console, with no CLI tools or third-party software required

text: Bucket policies support group-based access control using a principal's group memberships
quote: bucket policies now support group-based access control, letting you grant or restrict access based on a principal's group memberships rather than listing individual users

text: Exchange a CoreWeave API token for temporary object storage credentials through a container credentials endpoint
quote: you can now exchange that token directly for temporary AI Object Storage credentials through the container credentials endpoint

text: Bucket lifecycle policies support Expiration, NoncurrentVersionExpiration, and AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload
quote: supported lifecycle actions (Expiration, NoncurrentVersionExpiration, AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload)

text: HTTP precondition headers make object writes atomic and prevent overwrites without client-side locking
quote: Use HTTP precondition headers to make writes atomic and prevent accidental overwrites without requiring client-side locking.

text: RenameObject updates index entries instead of copying data, so renames finish in milliseconds at any object size
quote: RenameObject updates index entries instead of copying data, so rename operations complete in milliseconds regardless of object size.

text: Objects are classified as Hot, Warm, or Cold based on when they were last accessed
quote: they are classified as Hot, Warm, or Cold based on when they were last accessed

text: LOTA cache warming via a single HeadObject call, claimed to give a 30-50% faster first training epoch
quote: CoreWeave AI Object Storage now supports proactive LOTA cache warming with a single HeadObject call...Training jobs that start with a warm cache can see a 30-50% faster first epoch compared to cold reads.

text: LOTA accelerated object storage access works on CPU nodes and CPU-only clusters as well as GPU nodes
quote: CoreWeave's Local Object Transport Accelerator (LOTA) now runs on CPU Nodes in addition to GPU Nodes...LOTA is now available in clusters with any mix of Node types, including CPU-only clusters.

text: Billing insights show billable resource usage and consumption broken down by resource type
quote: Billing insights: View billable resource usage and consumption breakdowns by resource type.

text: Export usage programmatically with the FOCUS API (preview) or view cost and usage in Managed Grafana
quote: You can also export usage programmatically with the FOCUS API (Public Preview), or find your usage and costs in the Managed Grafana Cost and Usage product zone.

text: Grafana dashboards, logs, metrics, telemetry, and alerts for monitoring fleet hardware and workloads
quote: Grafana dashboards, logs, metrics, telemetry, and alerts for monitoring fleet hardware and workloads.

text: Mission Control Agent and MCP server can investigate your environment and make supported changes
quote: Mission Control Agent and the Mission Control MCP server for investigating your environment and making supported changes.
